record.paper_title: Offline Reinforcement Learning: Tutorial, Review, and Perspectives on Open Problems
record.original_question: How can model-based reinforcement learning accurately model Markov decision processes with very high-dimensional image observations and long horizons for offline control, given that current predictive models struggle with long-horizon prediction? Possible solutions may include better long-horizon observation models or hybrid model-based/model-free methods that use short rollouts or avoid predicting full observations.

evidence.quote: Modeling MDPs with very high-dimensional image observations and long horizons is a major open problem, and current predictive modeling methods generally struggle with long-horizon prediction. Hybrid methods that combine model-based and model-free learning, for example by utilizing short rollouts (Sutton, 1991; Janner et al., 2019) or avoiding prediction of full observations (Dosovitskiy and Koltun, 2016; Oh et al., 2017; Kahn et al., 2020) offer some promise in this area.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a Markov decision process (MDP) defined by the tuple (S, A, P, r, γ, ρ₀), where the state space S consists of very high-dimensional image observations (e.g., S ⊆ ℝ^d with d on the order of 10^4 or larger), A is an action space, P(s' | s, a) is an unknown transition kernel, r: S × A → ℝ is a reward function, γ ∈ (0,1) is a discount factor, and ρ₀ is an initial state distribution. In the offline setting, a learner is given a fixed dataset D = {(s_i, a_i, r_i, s'_i)} of transitions collected by one or more behavior policies, with no further interaction with the environment permitted. The goal is to output a policy π whose expected discounted return J(π) = E[Σ_{t=0}^∞ γ^t r(s_t, a_t)] approaches that of the optimal policy.

Develop a model-based offline reinforcement learning method that, using only D, learns a predictive model of the MDP accurate enough over long horizons (i.e., effective horizon H ≈ 1/(1−γ) large) to support reliable policy optimization in this image-observation regime, and provide finite-sample performance guarantees relating the learned policy's suboptimality to properties of D and the model class. Allowed approaches include: (i) direct long-horizon observation/dynamics models in pixel or latent space; (ii) hybrid model-based/model-free schemes using short rollouts branched from states in D; and (iii) methods that avoid predicting full observations, instead modeling rewards, value-relevant features, or measurement quantities. Establish whether such a method can match or exceed model-free offline RL baselines on long-horizon high-dimensional image-based control tasks while controlling distribution shift between the learned model's rollouts and the data.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of accurate long-horizon model learning from high-dimensional image observations for offline RL remains an active research area as of 2025–2026. While progress has been made (e.g., latent-space world models such as Dreamer variants and offline model-based methods like MOPO, MOReL, COMBO), no method is widely accepted as solving long-horizon image-based offline RL with strong guarantees, and recent surveys continue to list it as open.
